**[Experimental performance review bot]**

**Severity: medium**

The new loop fire-and-forgets one `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` call for every already-resolved restored session without a limiter, idle deferral, or grouping by equivalent assessment scope.

Reloading an Agents window with several persisted visible sessions immediately launches a full customization assessment for every restored session just as the workbench is restoring. Different workspace roots prevent MCP-scope coalescing, so a realistic multi-session grid fans out concurrent work.

**Suggested fix:** Queue these reports with bounded concurrency or defer them to idle, and coalesce assessments that share the same session type/workspace scope while preserving the required per-session telemetry semantics.

(Written by Copilot)

Addressed in cd4d9a1f199. All lifecycle migration assessments now flow through a service-owned limiter with concurrency 2. Restore still schedules one report per restored session, and the regression test verifies only two assessments run concurrently before the remaining session proceeds.

**[Experimental performance review bot]**

**Severity: medium**

After `restoreGrid`, all resolved sessions simultaneously start `computeMigrations`; late sessions do the same from `place`, with no queue or concurrency bound.

Restoring a window with several pinned sessions, especially across different workspaces, can produce an avoidable startup CPU/IPC spike and GC pressure while the restored UI is becoming interactive.

**Suggested fix:** Feed restore telemetry assessments through a small concurrency limiter or idle queue with restore-token cancellation; coalesce only assessments proven to share the same session/resource key, while still emitting the required per-session aggregate telemetry.

(Written by Copilot)

Addressed in cd4d9a1f199. Restore assessments are queued through a concurrency-2 limiter. Once a restored session is scheduled, later restore-token cancellation does not silently drop its per-session aggregate report. The restore test asserts bounded execution and all three reports.

**[Experimental performance review bot]**

**Severity: medium**

Startup restore now queues a full customization migration assessment for every restored session. Although each enqueue receives the restore cancellation token, queued and running factories discard it once admitted by the limiter.

If the user opens a session while startup is restoring several persisted sessions—especially while agent/customization state is cold—all stale restore assessments continue in the background. They consume filesystem/extension-provider I/O and MCP assessment CPU after the restore was abandoned, contending with the newly opened session and prolonging post-navigation activity.

**Suggested fix:** Recheck the restore token inside the limiter factory and pass it to `reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry`; make the MCP assessment wait cancellation-aware as well so already-running work releases its scope promptly. This preserves the concurrency limit and telemetry for restores that remain active while dropping only superseded work.

(Written by Copilot)

Addressed in ce5a6c70ba0. Limiter factories now recheck cancellation and pass the token through `reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry`/`computeMigrations`. Pending MCP support discovery uses `raceCancellationError`, so cancellation releases the support scope promptly. Active-session assessments use a separate token tied to active-session identity, preserving valid work across child-chat navigation while superseded restores cancel. Tests cover pending MCP cancellation/disposal and restore-to-child-chat deduplication.

🤖 **[P2] Same-plugin state changes can start overlapping README fetches and duplicate the rendered content.** The enablement autorun reruns `renderItem()` for the same item; each call clears once and starts this async fetch. When multiple requests resolve, they all pass the item-identity guard and append their Markdown. Please add cancellation or a render-generation guard and cover the same-item overlap in a test.

Valid and helpful. Same-item enablement changes could start multiple README reads, and item identity alone could not reject an older completion. I added a render-generation guard so only the latest render may append content, plus focused coverage for invalidating overlapping renders. The feedback could be slightly more prescriptive by noting that a generation guard is the broadly applicable fix here because both file and request-backed reads do not share one cancellable API.

🤖 **[P2] This async continuation can resume after the detail has been disposed.** In that case `setInput()` creates a new autorun, but the disposed `MutableDisposable` no longer owns/disposes it, so it remains live and repeatedly renders into detached DOM/disposed stores. `renderReadme()` has the same lifecycle gap after its awaited read: the generation/current checks still pass after disposal and the rendered Markdown is added to an already-disposed store. Add a disposal/cancellation guard after these awaits (or invalidate the render generation and clear `current` during disposal).

AI Review: Each non-browse search cancels the previous token, but this catch ignores cancellation and request identity. If an older fetch rejects after a newer request succeeds, it clears the newer marketplace results, shows a stale warning, and refilters; clearing the query also leaves pending work active. Cancel delayed and in-flight work when the query clears, and only mutate results or messages when the CTS, query, and browse mode still match the initiating request.

AI Review: The two preceding section-load awaits are not tied to the initiating navigation. If the user selects another section or view while either is pending, this stale continuation can still open the old plugin contribution and replace the newer destination. Track a navigation generation or cancellation token and recheck the requested section/view before calling showEmbeddedEditor.
